title: Syndicate Wars / Ghost in the shell inspired
author: KingQuiet880
selftext: Something I had in my head for a decade but just prototyped it now. Unity engine + Codex + Meshy. Game design and direction are mine mostly of how I felt playing Syndicate wars back in the days. I used AIs for grunt work and to fill the scene quickly. It is just mockup - do you think it is worth investing time with real team?

replies.author: KingQuiet880
replies.body:
* **Art direction:** Established a dark, retro-isometric cyberpunk style using visual references.
* **World building:** Built the district with streets, buildings, elevated walkways, stairs, shops, signage and street props.
* **Surface and lighting passes:** Added worn concrete, asphalt detail, reflections, neon lighting and adjustable bloom.
* **Character pipeline:** Generated and rigged characters in Meshy, rendered eight-direction animated sprites, and integrated them into Unity.
* **Living city systems:** Developed pedestrian navigation, crossings, traffic, civilian activities and security responses.
* **Player interaction:** Added driving, vehicle entry/exit, vaulting, ladder climbing and crouching.
* **Vehicle refinement:** Improved materials, scale, routing, obstacle handling and suspension.
* **Audio and storytelling:** Added ambient sound, looping music, volume controls and character communications through a shared intercom.
* **Iteration and testing:** Used screenshots and Play Mode feedback to refine visuals, fix collisions and navigation, and verify interactions.

  
As for prompts... to many even to make a coherent text. This was the one of early screenshots of the game so you can get the picture how many polish and refinement with very concrete ideas and visual direction it took to get it to that level seen in video.

comments.author: Eponymous-Username
comments.body:
I love it, but how about this? You control them with text and voice.

You direct the team. The AI interprets your instructions and turns it into actions on the part of the characters. You say, "go to the bank. Don't get spotted. There are two men on the roof", and the characters navigate there, spot the two men on the roof while acting nonchalant, then take up positions at the back door.

You say, "hack that panel", the characters converse briefly to figure out cover for the netrunner type, who enters stealth mode and gets to the panel.

Your characters are spotted and start taking fire. They take cover and return fire before asking for your orders. You tell them to get out of there, but as they're getting ready to leave you see their exits are cut off. You belay your order and say, "fight your way out".

I understand the challenges in implementing this, not least the performance and latency problems. Even worse if you want the team deliberating with one another, and feeding enough information to the LLM to enable it to make decisions about what each character should be doing via MCP would be difficult. Maybe you'd set up a two-tier brain for each character that would split instinct and action from higher-level planning, limiting calls to the LLM.

But, I know it's solvable, and just imagine the game you'd get from it!

replies.author: Eponymous-Username
replies.body:
Honestly, I think voice meshes so well with the strategy gaming format. It also introduces some realistic challenges, like learning to communicate clearly and dealing with misunderstood instructions.

The primary untraversible barrier has been converting player intent into instructions the game can understand and act upon. We bypass that with clicks, but LLMs and a tightly configured harness have removed the obstacle, and I really think the rest is an engineering problem to tune the harness.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
the aesthetic and style are great, and the visuals are impressive... i feel like you may be making the same mistake a lot of people in the sub make: 

style, aesthetic, even game systems aren't a game. they're things within a game 

a game is something you should, at least hypothetically, be able to prototype just with paper

  
i don't think anyone could honestly tell you whether or not this is worth investing in because what you've shown isn't really a game, just a very cool looking little sandox

what's the gameplay loop look like? is it a linear mission driven game like the old syndicate, with persistent characters that level up and become more machine than person over time? what does the player do in the game, aside from interacting with the systems - that is to say, they interact with the systems in order to do what? 

a visual demo like this is cool and important in its own kind of way, but can't really tell anyone whether the game itself is on the right track

replies.author: KingQuiet880
replies.body:
Thanks for the reply. Currently I am working on another RPG game with my team, so I prototyped this only as visual/minor gameplay mechanics showcase to see how people react to it. 

It is something I imagined for years, I would even try to make it as Syndicate 3 if EA doesn't hold a license for it. But gameplay loop would be based on classic Syndicate wars, with much more tactics, upgrading, 4k corporate domination. This particular scene was supposed to demonstrate escort duty, which allows control of 2 characters, climbing on buildings, preparing for possible ambush. Whole game could involve sneaking or frontal assaults, good guy vs greedy human shield kind of guy, depending on the style.  If I go with original story and lore, I always imagined that justification why it is always dark is because city is actually in a dome, because outside domes are wastelands due to global warming. So basically hubs are major cities protected by domes and you have missions where you actually go outside, which changes style from Syndicate to something else.   
  
Many possibilities for gameplay... but as I said, this is just a mockup.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Okay... but that doesn't really answer the question of what the game is. 'Tactics, upgrading, 4k corporate domination' describes genres, visuals and systems, not gameplay.

I'll give an example - Slay the Spire: 

 \- The player progresses through a map, encountering a variety of enemies in isolated duels that are resolved by playing cards. The player defeats enemies by doing damage to their finite pools of health, the player must survive while taking as little attritional damage as possible by playing defensive cards, player health is persistent across the run. The player must ultimately defeat Act bosses to win the game. The loop is: choose a node on the map to go to -> resolve the enounter at that node (an event, a fight or a rest) -> go back to the map and choose a new node. Repeat until reaching and defeating the Act bosses or until you run out of health and the game is over.

In your mind, at this early stage of imagining the game, what does your gameplay look like if you tried to use the above format to describe it?
